title: Gaussian Poincare Inequality (Sharp Constant 1)
body:
Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n and let f be locally Lipschitz with f and its gradient in L^2(gamma). Then Var_gamma(f) <= E_gamma[ |grad f|^2 ]. The constant 1 is SHARP and is attained exactly by the affine functions: for f(x) = a . x + b both sides equal |a|^2. The inequality is DIMENSION-FREE - the same constant 1 for every n - which is what makes it useful in high dimension, and it follows from the one-dimensional case by tensorization of the variance. It is strictly weaker than the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality, which implies it by applying the log-Sobolev inequality to 1 + eps f and expanding to second order in eps. Note the direction: the inequality bounds the variance by the gradient energy, so it gives concentration only at the level of variance, not exponential tails; exponential tails require the log-Sobolev inequality and the Herbst argument. [standard; e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 3.20]
gamma the standard Gaussian measure on R^n
f locally Lipschitz (or weakly differentiable) with f and grad f in L^2(gamma)
the constant 1 is sharp; there is no dimension dependence

metadata_json.proof_text: Expand in the orthonormal Hermite basis of L^2(gamma). For a multi-index alpha in the nonnegative integers to the n, let H_alpha(x) = prod_{i=1}^n h_{alpha_i}(x_i)/sqrt(alpha_i!) where h_k is the probabilists' Hermite polynomial, so that {H_alpha} is an orthonormal basis of L^2(gamma) and H_0 = 1. Write f = sum_alpha c_alpha H_alpha, so E[f] = c_0 and Var(f) = sum_{|alpha| >= 1} c_alpha^2, where |alpha| = alpha_1 + ... + alpha_n. The Hermite polynomials satisfy h_k' = k h_{k-1}, which in the normalised basis becomes the derivative relation d/dx_i H_alpha = sqrt(alpha_i) H_{alpha - e_i}. Hence grad f has i-th component sum_alpha c_alpha sqrt(alpha_i) H_{alpha - e_i}, and by orthonormality E[ |grad f|^2 ] = sum_i sum_alpha c_alpha^2 alpha_i = sum_alpha |alpha| c_alpha^2. Comparing termwise with Var(f) = sum_{|alpha| >= 1} c_alpha^2 and using |alpha| >= 1 on that index set gives Var(f) <= E|grad f|^2, with equality exactly when c_alpha = 0 for every alpha with |alpha| >= 2, that is when f is affine. The extension from smooth f to locally Lipschitz f is by mollification, using that Lipschitz functions are differentiable almost everywhere and that mollification does not increase the Lipschitz constant.
